c-tw-rate.label: One day's work: rate = 1 ÷ days
c-tw-rate.summary: Convert every time to a work rate and add rates when people work together.

c-tw-lcm.label: Total work as the LCM: units of work
c-tw-lcm.summary: Pick the total work as the LCM of the times; every rate becomes a whole number.

c-tw-pattern.label: People joining on a pattern or leaving midway
c-tw-pattern.summary: Work out one full cycle, count whole cycles, then finish the remainder.

q-tw-together.label: Working together for some time: fraction left
q-tw-together.summary: Add the rates, multiply by the time, subtract from 1.

q-tw-efficiency.label: Efficiency ratio against days
q-tw-efficiency.summary: Efficiency is inversely proportional to days; swap the ratio.

q-tw-leave.label: One worker or pump stops partway
q-tw-leave.summary: Work done by all, then the remainder done by the rest. Pipes and cisterns are the same.

q-tw-cycle.label: Workers join in a repeating pattern
q-tw-cycle.summary: One cycle's work, whole cycles, then a part-day.

c-tw-manday.label: Man-days: men × days (× hours) stays constant
c-tw-manday.summary: Work = people × days × hours. Convert women and children into men, then scale or split the work into stretches.

c-tw-wage.label: Wages shared in proportion to work done
c-tw-wage.summary: Money is shared by work done (rate × days), not by days alone.

q-tw-pairs.label: A + B, B + C and C + A given
q-tw-pairs.summary: Add the three pair rates and halve to get A + B + C; subtract a pair to isolate one worker.

q-tw-others.label: A takes k times as long as B and C together
q-tw-others.summary: 'k times as long as the others together' means that person does 1/(k + 1) of the combined rate.

q-tw-less.label: One worker takes d days less than another
q-tw-less.summary: 1/x + 1/(x + d) = 1/t. Try the options, or use t squared = product of the two gaps.

q-tw-hours.label: Different hours a day: work in man-hours
q-tw-hours.summary: Convert each time to total hours (days × hours a day), then use rates per hour.

q-tw-helpers.label: How many helpers to finish in a given time
q-tw-helpers.summary: Required rate minus the rate already there, divided by one helper's rate.

q-tw-undo.label: One person builds while another destroys
q-tw-undo.summary: Destroying is a negative rate: net work = builder's rate minus destroyer's rate for those days.

q-tw-alt.label: Workers take turns, one day each
q-tw-alt.summary: Work of one pair of days, count the whole pairs, then see who works next.

q-tw-manday.label: Men, women and boys on the same work
q-tw-manday.summary: Fix 1 man = × women = y boys, express everyone as men, then use man-days.

q-tw-mdh.label: Scaling men, days and hours
q-tw-mdh.summary: men × days × hours ÷ work is the same for both cases; use it to find the unknown.

q-tw-teams.label: Men join or leave, or work is split in stretches
q-tw-teams.summary: Work out how many man-days are done, subtract from the total, and divide by the new strength.

q-tw-more.label: Extra men finish the job earlier
q-tw-more.summary: Total man-days stay fixed: n × d = (n + k)(d − e).

q-tw-wage.label: Share a payment between workers
q-tw-wage.summary: Shares are in the ratio of work done: rate × days worked for each.

c-tw-pipe.label: Pipes and cisterns: filling and emptying
c-tw-pipe.summary: A filling pipe is a positive rate, an emptying pipe or a leak is a negative rate. Add the signed rates, then divide the work by the net rate.

q-pc-together.label: Two or three filling pipes together
q-pc-together.summary: Add the rates; or use product ÷ sum for two pipes.

q-pc-three.label: Filling pipes and an emptying pipe, all open
q-pc-three.summary: Net rate = fillers − drain. Check the sign: a negative net means the tank empties.

q-pc-leak.label: A leak makes the filling slower
q-pc-leak.summary: Leak rate = normal rate − rate with the leak; it empties a full tank in 1 ÷ that.

q-pc-closed.label: A pipe is opened or closed after some time
q-pc-closed.summary: Work out the part filled in each stretch, subtract from the whole, and finish at the new rate (add clock times at the end).

q-pc-alt.label: Pipes opened alternately
q-pc-alt.summary: Net work of one pair of minutes, count whole pairs, and check whether the last minute is a filling one.

q-pc-diameter.label: Pipes of different diameters
q-pc-diameter.summary: Flow is proportional to the cross-section area, so to the square of the diameter.

q-pc-volume.label: Capacity in litres, drops and fractions of a tank
q-pc-volume.summary: Turn the given litres into a fraction of the tank (or the reverse); keep every rate in one unit.

q-pc-pumps.label: Number of pumps against time
q-pc-pumps.summary: Pumps × hours × days is fixed for the same job.

q-pc-general.label: General formulas and 'faster by' questions
q-pc-general.summary: xy ÷ (y − x) for a filler and a drain; test options for 'takes d hours less' questions.

formulas.text: Efficiency ∝ 1 ÷ days: efficiency A : B = days B : days A
Total work = LCM of the times; rate = LCM ÷ days
Cycle work = sum of the work done over one repeat; days = whole cycles × length + part of the next
formulas.note: Finish inside a day by dividing the remaining work by that day's rate.

formulas.text: A + B + C = (sum of the three pair rates) ÷ 2
Work = men × days × hours, so M1 D1 H1 ÷ W1 = M2 D2 H2 ÷ W2
formulas.note: Men and days are inverse; work is direct.

formulas.text: Share of money = share of work = rate × days worked
formulas.note: Wages per day are equal only if the workers are equally efficient.

formulas.text: A takes k times as long as the others together: A's rate = total rate ÷ (k + 1)
formulas.note: Two or three such statements fix every rate.

formulas.text: Net rate = (sum of filling rates) − (sum of emptying rates); time = 1 ÷ net rate
formulas.note: A negative net rate means the tank empties.

formulas.text: Filler x hours, drain y hours (y > x): time to fill = xy ÷ (y − x)
Leak: with-leak time t2 > normal time t1, the leak empties in t1 t2 ÷ (t2 − t1)
formulas.note: 9 h normal, 10 h with the leak: 9 × 10 ÷ 1 = 90 h.
Double the diameter and the flow becomes 4 times.

q-tw-together.cue: 'X takes … days, Y takes … days. They work together for … days. What fraction remains?'
q-tw-together.standard: Rates 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per day; in 3 days 15/36 = 5/12 is done; remaining 1 − 5/12 = 7/12.
q-tw-together.fast: LCM 36: X = 3, Y = 2, together 5 a day; 3 days = 15 of 36, so 21/36 = 7/12 is left.
q-tw-together.eliminate: Together they need under 7.2 days, so 3 days is less than half the work done: the remaining fraction must be above 1/2, which strikes 1/3 and 5/12.
traps: Giving the fraction done (5/12) rather than the fraction left.
Adding the days instead of the rates.
Mixing both times into one rate before taking the LCM.

q-tw-efficiency.cue: 'The ratio of efficiencies of A and B is 4 : 3. If A takes 18 days, how long does B take?'
q-tw-efficiency.standard: Efficiency is inverse to days: A : B days = 3 : 4; A = 18 days is 3 parts, so 1 part = 6 and B = 24 days.
q-tw-efficiency.fast: The slower worker (B) takes more days: 18 × 4/3 = 24.
q-tw-efficiency.eliminate: B is less efficient, so takes more than 18 days; and 18 × 4/3 is exactly 24. Strike options that make B faster.
traps: Multiplying by 3/4 (13.5) instead of 4/3.
Treating the ratio as the days ratio.

q-tw-leave.cue: Several pumps or workers, one leaves after some time, how much more time to finish?
q-tw-leave.standard: All three: 1/5 + 1/7 + 1/10 = 31/70 per hour. In 1.5 h they do 93/140, leaving 47/140. A + B = 12/35 = 48/140 per hour, so the time is 47/48 hour.
q-tw-leave.fast: LCM 70: A = 14, B = 10, C = 7, all three 31 per hour; 1.5 h = 46.5 done, 23.5 left; A + B = 24, so 23.5 ÷ 24 = 47/48 h.
q-tw-leave.eliminate: After C stops, A + B still does 24 of 70 per hour, and well under half the work remains, so the extra time is under 1 hour. That strikes 43/25 hours and leaves 47/48, 45/41 or 1/2.
traps: Using all three rates for the remaining work.
Forgetting the first 1.5 hours.
Adding the three times together.

q-tw-cycle.cue: 'X works every day, Y and Z join X every third day.' How long to finish?
q-tw-cycle.standard: LCM 120: X 6, Y 3, Z 2 per day. Three days of the cycle: 6 + 6 + 11 = 23. Five cycles = 15 days = 115 units; the 5 left need 5/6 of the 16th day (X alone does 6). Total 15 5/6 days.
q-tw-cycle.fast: 23 units every 3 days, so 115 by day 15; the last 5 at X's rate of 6 per day is 5/6.
q-tw-cycle.eliminate: The average rate is under 8 a day, so 120 units take more than 15 days; strike any answer under 15. And the pattern ends mid-day, so a whole-number answer such as 18 days is too long.
traps: Counting the extra day as a whole day (16).
Using all three workers on the last day.
Taking 20 ÷ (1/20 + 1/40 + 1/60) with everyone working daily.

q-tw-pairs.cue: 'A and B in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, C and A in 20 days. All three together?'
q-tw-pairs.fast: LCM 60: the pairs do 5, 4 and 3 units, which add to 12, so one of each does 6 a day: 60 ÷ 6 = 10 days.
q-tw-pairs.eliminate: All three together must beat every pair, so the answer is below 12 days; strike any option at or above the smallest pair time.
traps: Forgetting to halve the sum of the pair rates.
Adding the three pair times.
Finding A + B + C but answering for one worker.

q-tw-others.cue: 'B takes three times as long as A and C together, and C twice as long as A and B together. All three together take 10 days.'
q-tw-others.standard: B is 1/4 and C is 1/3 of the total rate 1/10, so A = 1/10 × (1 − 1/4 − 1/3) = 1/24: 24 days.
q-tw-others.fast: Take 120 units: all three do 12 a day. B does 1/4 of that (3), C does 1/3 (4), so A does 5 a day and takes 120 ÷ 5 = 24 days.
q-tw-others.eliminate: A alone must take longer than the 10 days the three need together, and A is the fastest of the three here, so the answer lies between 10 and 30: strike 5, 8 and any option above B or C's time.
traps: Using 1/3 instead of 1/(3 + 1) for 'three times as long'.
Subtracting the fractions from 1 without scaling by the combined rate.

q-tw-less.cue: 'A takes 10 days less than B. Together they take 12 days. How long does B take?'
q-tw-less.standard: 1/x + 1/(x + 10) = 1/12 gives x² − 14x − 120 = 0, so x = 20 and B takes 30 days.
q-tw-less.fast: Test option pairs: B = 30 means A = 20 and 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12 ✓. If only 'together' time t is asked after extra hours a and b: t² = a × b.
q-tw-less.eliminate: Each worker takes more than the combined time, so A is above 12 days and B above 22; strike options that break this.
traps: Taking A = B − 10 but adding the days instead of the rates.
Answering for A when B is asked.

q-tw-hours.cue: 'Working 7 hours a day, A takes 6 days, B takes 8 days. Together, working 8 hours a day?'
q-tw-hours.standard: A needs 42 hours, B needs 56 hours: together 1/42 + 1/56 = 1/24 per hour, so 24 hours = 3 days at 8 hours a day.
q-tw-hours.fast: Total hours first (days × hours), then LCM 168: A = 4, B = 3, together 7 an hour: 24 hours.
q-tw-hours.eliminate: Together they need fewer days than the faster worker alone at 8 hours a day (under 5.25 days).
traps: Combining the days (6 and 8) without allowing for the changed hours.
Dividing 24 hours by 7 instead of 8.

q-tw-helpers.cue: 'A man, a woman and a boy do a job in 3, 4 and 12 days. How many boys must assist 1 man and 1 woman to finish in 1/4 of a day?'
q-tw-helpers.standard: Needed rate = 4 a day (one job in 1/4 day). Man + woman = 1/3 + 1/4 = 7/12. Boys give 4 − 7/12 = 41/12, and each does 1/12, so 41 boys.
q-tw-helpers.fast: LCM 12: man 4, woman 3, boy 1 a day. The job (12 units) in 1/4 day needs 48 a day; man + woman give 7, so 41 boys.
q-tw-helpers.eliminate: The man and woman supply only 7 of the 48 units a day needed, so most of the work falls on boys: the answer is large, strike small options.
traps: Taking the needed rate as 1/4 instead of 1 ÷ (1/4) = 4.
Forgetting to subtract what the man and woman already do.

q-tw-undo.cue: 'A builds in 8 days which B destroys in 3 days. A worked 6 days, the last 2 with B destroying. How many more days must A work?'
q-tw-undo.standard: LCM 24: A builds 3 a day, B destroys 8 a day. Four plain days = 12; two days with B = 2 × (3 − 8) = −10. Net 2, so 22 remain: 22 ÷ 3 = 7 1/3 days.
q-tw-undo.fast: Treat the destroyer as a negative rate, then continue with A alone.
q-tw-undo.eliminate: Net progress is tiny after the destruction, so the extra time is nearly the whole job (about 8 days): strike options under 7.
traps: Adding B's rate instead of subtracting it.
Forgetting the days A worked before the destruction began.

q-tw-alt.cue: 'A and B take 9 and 12 days. They work alternately a day each, A first. How long to finish?'
q-tw-alt.standard: LCM 36: A = 4, B = 3. A pair of days = 7. Five pairs (10 days) = 35, then A needs 1 more unit: 1/4 day. Total 10 1/4 days.
q-tw-alt.fast: Find the whole pairs, then check who works next and finish the remainder at his rate.
q-tw-alt.eliminate: A pair of days does 7 of the 36 units, so the job needs just over 10 days (35 units in 10 days, with a part-day left): strike every option below 10.
traps: Taking the remaining work at the wrong person's rate.
Counting a part-day as a full day.

q-tw-manday.cue: '12 men or 20 women do a job in 15 and 12 days. 5 men and 5 women together?'
q-tw-manday.standard: 12 men × 15 = 180 man-days = 20 women × 12 = 240 woman-days, so 1 man = 4/3 women. Convert everyone to one kind, then divide the total work by their combined rate.
q-tw-manday.fast: Fix 1 man = x women, express all in the smaller unit, then use total units ÷ combined units per day.
q-tw-manday.eliminate: A mixed group of equal numbers of two kinds works at a speed between the two kinds, so the time lies between the two single-type times.
traps: Treating men and women as equal.
Taking the 'or' as 'and' (adding the times).

q-tw-mdh.cue: '(x + 4) men in (x + 5) days = (x − 5) men in (x + 20) days. Find x.' or 'm men, d days, h hours a day'.
q-tw-mdh.standard: Men × days (× hours) is the same for equal work: (x + 4)(x + 5) = (x − 5)(x + 20) gives x = 20.
q-tw-mdh.eliminate: x must exceed 5, since (x − 5) men must be positive; strike small options first.
traps: Setting up men ÷ days instead of men × days.
Forgetting the hours a day.

q-tw-teams.cue: '40 men can do a job in 40 days, but at the end of every 10th day 5 men leave. How long?'
q-tw-teams.standard: Total 40 × 40 = 1,600 man-days. Day-blocks of 10 days do 400, 350, 300, 250, 200 (total 1,500 in 50 days); the last 100 with 15 men takes 6 2/3 days: 56 2/3.
q-tw-teams.fast: Write man-days per stretch and subtract from the total until what is left fits inside one stretch.
q-tw-teams.eliminate: Strength only falls, so the job takes more than 40 days: strike 40 and below.
traps: Forgetting that the strength keeps falling every stretch.
Counting the last part-stretch as a full stretch.

q-tw-more.cue: 'Some men finish in 30 days; with 5 more men, 10 days less. How many men at the start?'
q-tw-more.fast: The days drop in ratio 3 : 2, so the men rise in ratio 2 : 3: the 5 extra men are the 1 part, so the start was 2 parts = 10.
q-tw-more.eliminate: Extra men cut the time by a third, so the extra men are half of the original: the original is 2 × 5 = 10.
traps: Writing n/30 = (n + 5)/20 (direct instead of inverse).
Answering with n + 5.

q-tw-wage.cue: 'A and B finish a job in 15 and 10 days for ₹ 30,000. What is A's share?'
q-tw-wage.fast: Share ∝ rate, and rate ∝ 1/days: the ratio of shares is the reverse of the days ratio, 10 : 15 = 2 : 3.
q-tw-wage.eliminate: A is the slower worker, so A gets less than half: strike any option above half the total.
traps: Sharing in the ratio of the days (15 : 10) instead of the reverse.
Ignoring a helper's work when three workers are involved.

q-pc-together.cue: 'Pipes A and B fill a tank in 20 and 30 minutes. Opened together?'
q-pc-together.fast: Two pipes: 20 × 30 ÷ (20 + 30) = 12. If one pipe is k times as fast, together they have (k + 1) parts.
q-pc-together.eliminate: Together they must beat the faster pipe alone: under 20 minutes; and they cannot do better than half of it (10 minutes).
traps: Adding the times (50).
Averaging the times (25).
Mixing hours and minutes in the same sum.

q-pc-three.cue: 'Two pipes fill in 3 and 4 hours, a waste pipe empties in 2 hours. All three open?'
q-pc-three.standard: LCM 12: fillers 4 + 3, drain 6, so the net is +1 unit an hour: 12 hours.
q-pc-three.fast: LCM of all the times; fillers positive, drain negative; total ÷ net.
q-pc-three.eliminate: If the drain is faster than the fillers together the tank never fills; otherwise the time is longer than the faster filler alone.
traps: Adding the drain's rate instead of subtracting it.
Ignoring the sign and getting a negative time.

q-pc-leak.cue: 'A pipe fills a tank in 9 hours; with a leak it takes 10. The leak empties it in?'
q-pc-leak.eliminate: The leak must be much slower than the pipe, since it only adds one hour of delay: strike answers near 10.
traps: Answering 1 hour (the extra time).
Dividing by the sum instead of the difference.

q-pc-closed.cue: 'Both pipes opened; after 7 minutes a third pipe opened (or one closed). Total time?'
q-pc-closed.standard: LCM units; work done in the first stretch; remaining ÷ the new net rate; add the stretches.
q-pc-closed.fast: For a pipe that runs the whole time, its share is time ÷ its own time; the other pipe fills the rest.
q-pc-closed.eliminate: Check the final total exceeds the time already run; for clock-time answers add to the start time at the end.
traps: Giving the extra time when the total is asked (or the reverse).
Letting the closed pipe keep running.

q-pc-alt.cue: 'A fills in 20 minutes, B empties in 30. Opened for one minute each in turn.'
q-pc-alt.standard: LCM 60: A +3, B −2, a pair nets 1. After 57 pairs 57 units; the next filling minute adds 3 and finishes: 115 minutes.
q-pc-alt.fast: Do not wait for the last pair: stop at the filling minute that completes the job.
q-pc-alt.eliminate: The answer is a little under (net per pair) × (number of pairs) ÷ 1: the full-pairs figure (120 minutes) is too long, because the finishing minute is a filling one.
traps: Using the pair rate all the way (120 minutes).
Forgetting which pipe starts.

q-pc-diameter.cue: 'A pipe of diameter d empties a tank in 40 minutes. A pipe of 2d?'
q-pc-diameter.standard: Area ∝ d²: the 2d pipe has 4 times the flow, so 40 ÷ 4 = 10 minutes.
q-pc-diameter.fast: Square the ratio of the diameters and divide the time by it.
q-pc-diameter.eliminate: Doubling the size cannot just halve the time: strike the 20-minute answer.
traps: Taking flow ∝ diameter.
Multiplying the time instead of dividing.

q-pc-volume.cue: '3/4 of the tank is full; 30 litres taken out empties it. Capacity?'
q-pc-volume.standard: Convert the given litres into a fraction of the tank, then scale up; keep litres, minutes and hours in one unit.
q-pc-volume.eliminate: The capacity must exceed the water in the tank: strike options below it.
traps: Dividing by 3/4 the wrong way round.
Mixing litres with ml or cm³.

q-pc-pumps.cue: '12 pumps working 6 hours a day empty a reservoir in 15 days. How many pumps at 9 hours a day in 12 days?'
q-pc-pumps.eliminate: More hours a day need fewer pumps, but fewer days need more: check the two effects cancel in the right direction.
traps: Setting up a direct instead of an inverse proportion.

q-pc-general.cue: 'A pipe fills in x hours, another empties in y hours (y > x). Both open?' or 'the faster takes 10 hours less'.
q-pc-general.standard: 1/x − 1/y = (y − x)/xy, so the time is xy ÷ (y − x).
q-pc-general.fast: Plug x = 2, y = 3: the answer must be 6.
q-pc-general.eliminate: The answer must be positive when y > x: strike (x − y).
traps: Swapping x and y in the denominator.

pyqs.text: X is able to complete a task in 12 days, while Y takes 18 days to finish the same task. If they work together for 3 days, what fraction of the work will still remain?
solution: LCM of 12 and 18 = 36 units: X does 3 a day, Y does 2 a day.
Together 5 a day; in 3 days 15 units of 36 are done.
Remaining = 21/36 = 7/12.
pyqs.trick: Take total work 36; the pair does 5 a day.

pyqs.text: Three pumps A, B and C fill a reservoir in 5, 7 and 10 hours. All three work together for 1.5 hours, then C is closed. How much more time is needed to fill the reservoir?
solution: LCM 70: A = 14, B = 10, C = 7 per hour; all three = 31 per hour.
In 1.5 hours: 46.5 units, so 23.5 are left.
A + B = 24 per hour, so time = 23.5 ÷ 24 = 47/48 hour.
pyqs.trick: Total 70: 46.5 done, 23.5 left, A + B do 24.

pyqs.text: X, Y and Z can complete a project in 20, 40 and 60 days. X works every day, while Y and Z join X every third day. How long will it take to finish the project?
solution: LCM 120: X = 6, Y = 3, Z = 2 per day.
A 3-day cycle: 6 + 6 + (6 + 3 + 2) = 23 units. Five cycles (15 days) = 115 units.
5 units left at X's rate of 6 per day = 5/6 day. Total = 15 5/6 days.
(The paper prints option (a) oddly, as '12 7/2 days'; either way it is not the answer.)

pyqs.text: The ratio of efficiencies of workers A and B is 4 : 3. If A can finish a task in 18 days, in how many days will B finish the same task alone?
solution: Efficiency and time are inversely proportional, so A : B days = 3 : 4.
3 parts = 18 days, 1 part = 6, so B = 4 × 6 = 24 days.
pyqs.trick: B is slower, so 18 × 4/3 = 24.

pyqs.text: A can do a piece of work in 6 days and B in 9 days. How many days will both take together to complete the work?
solution: Rates: 1/6 + 1/9 = 5/18 per day.
Time = 18/5 = 3.6 days.
pyqs.trick: Product ÷ sum: 6 × 9 ÷ 15 = 3.6.

solution: Take total work 60 units: A does 4, B does 3 per day.
In 4 days they do 28 units, so 32 are left.

pyqs.text: A can cultivate 2/5th of a land in 6 days and B can cultivate 1/3th of the same land in 10 days. Working together A and B can cultivate 4/5th of the land in:
solution: A alone takes 6 × 5/2 = 15 days; B alone takes 10 × 3 = 30 days.
Together rate = 1/15 + 1/30 = 1/10 per day.
4/5 of the land takes 8 days.

solution: B takes 9 days.
Together in one day: 1/18 + 1/9 = 3/18 = 1/6.

solution: Take total work 24 units: rates 1, 4 and 2 per day.
Together 7 units a day, so 24/7 = 3 3/7 days.
pyqs.trick: Total = LCM 24; add the unit rates.
